key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell designs and pinpoint the most influential layer properties for high-efficiency devices.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design map for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL choices in conventional and lead-free double perovskite solar cells without exhaustive simulation or experimentation.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen configurations.
Used SHAP to identify the most important descriptors: HTL band gap, absorber band gap, and ETL electron affinity.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation, and the best verified architectures reached 28.85% PCE and 28.62% PCE in full SCAPS-1D simulations.
watch_item: The ML predictions depend on the simulated design space and may not fully capture real-device fabrication effects, defect variability, or stability constraints.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
